title: Don't Hold the Guard
goal: Extract the value from the Mutex before awaiting so the future stays Send.
hints: `std::sync::MutexGuard` does not implement Send, so keeping it alive across .await poisons the future.
Dereference *m.lock().unwrap() immediately to copy the i32 and drop the MutexGuard at the end of the statement.
explanation: Holding a `std::sync::MutexGuard` across an .await makes the future non-Send because MutexGuard cannot cross thread boundaries (E0277). Dereferencing *m.lock().unwrap() copies the inner i32 into val and drops the MutexGuard at the end of the let statement before fetch() is called. Trying to take a mutable reference &mut *m.lock().unwrap() fails with E0716 because the temporary MutexGuard drops while borrowed. Calling .unwrap() on a future fails with E0599 because futures are not Results.
